# Doctor: mapping-config diagnostics with offline-always / live-drift-degrades portability

## Context / Problem

The mapping seam (S1–S8) adds a hand-editable `[mapping]` config surface. Two failure classes
need surfacing before a reconcile silently drifts:

- **Internally-invalid config** — already fail-closed via `MappingConfigError`: a non-integer
  `hierarchy` / malformed block fail at LOAD; out-of-vocabulary and unmapped-non-skipped values
  fail in the `config` resolvers. Doctor surfaces these as **error** findings.
- **Live drift** — internally valid but disagreeing with live Jira (a mapped status/type/link
  Jira dropped). Surface when Jira is reachable; degrade cleanly when not.

`rebar doctor` is the existing diagnostic home, so extend it. It must stay portable: it runs
where the optional **`jira-datacenter`** extra is absent and no credentials are set — offline
checks always run; the live-drift check degrades to an `unavailable` finding, mirroring
`rebar metrics` (`docs/user-guide.md`).

## Approach

Add a mapping-diagnostics function to `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py`, wired into `scan`.
Mapping findings go in their **own list** (as for scan-dirty/lock reports), are rendered and
folded into the exit code, and kept **out of** `run_repair`'s iteration — so `doctor.scan()`'s
blocking-edge finding contract (and `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py`) is unchanged.

- **Offline checks (always run, stdlib-only, no Jira import):** first call
  `mapping_config.load_mapping_config` inside `try/except MappingConfigError` — a load-time
  failure (non-integer hierarchy, or a malformed axis/vocabulary block) becomes one **error**
  finding whose `detail` is the `MappingConfigError` message verbatim — it already frames the key
  in either prefix format (`[mapping.<where>]:` for axis/hierarchy/layer, `[mapping].<where>:`
  for vocabulary), so no brittle parsing — and the per-key pass is skipped. On a successful load, enumerate `config.projects` **union the default layer** and, per
  key, run the provider-neutral `config` resolvers — `effective_status_map`, `effective_type_map`,
  `assert_type_decisions_complete`, `effective_link_map` — which inject the built-in
  `MappingLayer` + `Capability`, import `mapping_config` lazily, and are stdlib-only at import
  (never `adapters.jira*`); a resolve-time `MappingConfigError` (out-of-vocabulary,
  unmapped-non-skipped) → an **error** finding naming the key (non-zero exit). On the same per-key pass, one genuinely *soft* problem — an all-empty `projects.<KEY>` block
  (likely a stub) — is a **warning** naming the key, not an error.
- **Live-drift check (best-effort, degrades):** run only when the `jira-datacenter` extra is
  importable — gated through `rebar._optional.capability_installed("jira_datacenter")` — AND
  credentials resolve. On the available path, reuse S8's read-only probe reader
  (`mapping_probe.build_probe`) and diff configured vs observed vocabulary, one finding per
  divergence on the axes the reader observes — **status, type, link** (a configured value absent
  from Jira's set).
  Hierarchy is deliberately **excluded** from the live diff: `build_probe` resolves Data Center,
  where `mapping_probe._hierarchy` is always empty (`hierarchyLevel` is Cloud-only) — so a
  hierarchy divergence is structurally undetectable here (offline hierarchy validity still
  covered above). When the
  extra is absent, OR the resolved PAT is empty (`JIRA_PAT` unset — `resolve_jira_datacenter_settings`
  returns `pat=""`), OR settings resolution raises `ConfigError` (fail-loud on a malformed
  `[tool.rebar.reconciler]`), OR the probe
  transport raises or times out (the probe call runs under a doctor-side bounded wall-clock
  timeout — a daemon worker thread with `result(timeout=…)`, bound a module constant (default
  10s), since S8's `build_client_from_settings` sets none; a timed-out thread is abandoned and
  doctor returns promptly with `unavailable`), emit a single `unavailable` finding
  ("live mapping-drift check skipped: <reason>") and return success — never raise. The Jira import
  and probe construction happen lazily behind the guard, wrapped so every degradation cause
  folds into the one `unavailable` finding.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py` — new mapping-diagnostics function (own findings list); the
  `capability_installed("jira_datacenter")` guard and lazy Jira import.
- `docs/user-guide.md` — document the offline error/warning findings and the `unavailable`
  live-drift convention.
- Reuses S1's `mapping_config` (via `config` resolvers) and S8's `mapping_probe.build_probe`.
- Out of scope: `--repair` for mapping config (report-only); Jira as a hard doctor dependency;
  the live-drift **true path against real Jira** — transport is S8's proven read-only probe
  reader (covered by S8), so this child proves the diff logic via an injected vocabulary and
  treats the real-transport path as not-applicable.

## Testing

- **Unit (offline tier), no Jira import:** temp config with (a) valid mapping → no findings;
  (b) each error-class problem — a load-time one in each message format (non-integer hierarchy
  `[mapping.<where>]:`, and a malformed vocabulary list `[mapping].<where>:`) and a resolve-time
  one (out-of-vocabulary value, unmapped-non-skipped type) → an **error** finding whose detail
  carries the key + non-zero exit; (c) an all-empty `projects.<KEY>` block → a **warning**. Asserts
  no `adapters.jira` import on this path. Oracle: finding list + exit code.
- **Unit (portability tier):** force the guard false (monkeypatch `capability_installed` for
  `"jira_datacenter"`) → exactly one `unavailable` finding, success exit, no Jira import. Oracle:
  the single finding + zero exit.
- **Unit (degradation causes):** guard true; drive each cause — empty resolved PAT, a
  `ConfigError` from settings resolution, and a slow/hanging probe reader exceeding the
  doctor-side timeout — each folds into one `unavailable` finding with the matching reason +
  success exit. Oracle: the finding + reason + zero exit.
- **Unit (live-drift tier), injected transport:** inject a fake probe reader whose vocabulary
  diverges on status, type, and link → one drift finding per divergence naming the axis + absent
  value. No live Jira. Oracle: the per-axis finding set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `rebar doctor` on a valid `[mapping]` config with the `jira-datacenter` extra absent
  succeeds and emits exactly one `unavailable` live-drift finding — portability-tier test (guard
  forced false via `capability_installed`, no Jira import, zero exit).
- [x] Each offline error-class problem yields an **error** finding whose detail carries the key
  + non-zero exit: both load-error message formats (non-integer hierarchy `[mapping.<where>]:`
  and malformed vocabulary `[mapping].<where>:`) surfaced verbatim, plus the resolve-time errors
  (out-of-vocabulary value, unmapped-non-skipped type) reached by enumerating `config.projects`
  + the default layer per key — offline-tier test asserting the `MappingConfigError`-derived
  finding.
- [x] An all-empty `projects.<KEY>` stub yields a **warning** finding naming the key (not an
  error, not a non-zero exit) — offline-tier test.
- [x] Each degradation cause — extra absent, empty resolved PAT (`JIRA_PAT` unset), a
  `ConfigError` from settings resolution, and a slow/hanging probe exceeding the doctor-side
  timeout — folds into a single `unavailable` finding + reason + success exit — portability and
  degradation-cause tests.
- [x] With a fake probe reader injected, each configured-vs-observed divergence on status, type,
  and link yields a drift finding naming the axis + absent value — live-drift-tier test.
  Hierarchy is excluded by design (the reused Data Center probe never observes `hierarchyLevel`).
- [x] `docs/user-guide.md` documents the new mapping diagnostics.

All four tiers run in-process, no live Jira, no specific CI provider — satisfying
`project.portability`.
